description: Southern Thai prayer hall under a large ribbed dome with smaller corner domes and a single slender minaret alongside.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Rectangular prayer hall under one large ribbed onion dome on a drum, four smaller matching domes at the roof corners, a single slender tapering minaret alongside topped with a small domed balcony and a crescent finial, arched arcade of pointed horseshoe arches along the entrance front, low boundary wall with an arched gateway Materials: White and pale green painted render with damp staining low on the walls, green glazed dome ribs, gold crescent finials, weathered whitewash on the boundary wall, dark mildew streaks under the eaves.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.81 -- not a pass self-score, and held down almost entirely by the silhouette layer at 0.74: the declared 18 m on a 14 x 16 footprint is 57% taller relative to plan than the Meshy proxy reads the same plate, which is a declaration the registry notes make explicitly and defend. Re-normalised by width, the two agree to 1.6%. 12,882/32,000 triangles, 14/24 draw calls, 6/16 materials, 14/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: One melon-ribbed dome of 22 ribs over the hall, and one minaret standing at x=-5.75 against a hall half-width of 4.60, reaching the declared 18.00 m exactly.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes say neither element works alone, and the first build proved it: with the minaret at x=-5.05 its shaft vanished behind the great dome from every review angle and the prop read as a domed box. Moving it clear of the hall restored the pairing. The ribs are generated geometry -- a radius modulated AROUND the axis, which no lathe can do, because a lathe revolves one profile at one radius per height. A smooth green hemisphere reads as a water tank.

featureReviews.evidence: Five Moorish arches across the hall front -- shoulder stepping out at the spring, round lobe, ogee point -- three doorways with a dark panel behind each and two blind niches with a green field and a raised inner panel, every surround standing proud of its bay and reaching to within 1.1 m of the parapet band. The same arch is cut through the gate block.
featureReviews.notes: The arch had to be written for this prop. The half-round sweep already in the toolkit is the wrong arch and reads as a railway viaduct; the two-centred pointed arch is one of the few things on a whitewashed box that says mosque at all. The dark behind stands 0.02 m PROUD of the wall rather than recessed into it -- the hall is a solid mass -- and at depth 0.06 its front face sat in the parapet's own z=4.28 plane over 5.35 m2, five times over; 0.05 clears it.

featureReviews.evidence: Four small ribbed domes on their own drums at the roof corners with gilt spikes, and over the great dome and the minaret the plate's ornament: cap, ball, neck, bulb, spike and a flat crescent with its horns to the upper right.
featureReviews.notes: The corner drums took two rounds of coplanar fixing: level with the great dome's drum they shared four planes with it, and level with the deck slab they shared four with the deck instead. They now sit below both. The crescent needed a stem -- it sits on the axis and every review viewpoint is off-axis, so without one the gap read as a detached ornament floating beside the minaret rather than as the top of the finial.

featureReviews.evidence: Turntable gate run with --allow-holes and the measurement that justifies it.
featureReviews.notes: The gate flags enclosed background on every azimuth -- 9,520 to 13,561 pixels at mean thicknesses of 40 to 84 px. Unlike every other use of that flag in this kit these are not anti-aliased edges one pixel thick: they are the COURTYARD. A walled compound has real open ground between its enclosure wall and its hall, and from any three-quarter view the silhouette encloses that background on all four sides. The gate's assumption -- that a prop's outline contains no background -- does not hold for an enclosure, and the flag is set on that finding rather than to get past an unexplained failure.

featureReviews.evidence: Six materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate.
featureReviews.notes: Three findings worth keeping. This plate's dirt runs the OPPOSITE way from every other prop in the batch -- rain wash streaks the render from the coping DOWN, measuring #818485 near the parapet against #B2B2AE lower -- so the vertex tint ramps upward, and authoring it the usual way round would have been visibly wrong. The parapet band admits no pure crop at plate resolution: it is 22 pixels tall with white coping either side, so the material takes the palette entry #90957B the extraction separates out rather than the mixed mean #9E9F90. And the dome striping is a per-vertex multiplier in LINEAR space, not the sRGB the crops were measured in -- fed the sRGB ratio the dome rendered almost uniformly pale.

name: Mosque
notes: Most numerous in the southern provinces, and the recognisable pairing is one large ribbed dome plus a single slender minaret standing clear of the hall -- that two-part silhouette is what reads at distance and neither element works alone. Declared at 18 m tall, well above the building-part category's 8 m prior, because the minaret rather than the hall sets the height. Green and white are the usual colours and the prompt names both so the plate does not come back in the gold and orange of a Buddhist temple. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.
